cards.text: For 40 years Malaysia waived taxes to win factories. A global 15% floor, in force since January 2025, means the tax it skips is now collected abroad.
cards.sub: When a company's Malaysian rate falls below 15%, a top-up is owed somewhere. Malaysia rewrote its law to claim it before another country could.
sources: MIDA, Implementation of GMT in Malaysia (FY from 1 Jan 2025; 15% ETR); OECD Pillar Two GloBE Model Rules

cards.h: A firm taxed below 15% in Malaysia now owes a top-up to reach it. If Putrajaya does not collect that gap, the company's home country can.
cards.s: The Finance Act 2023 brought in a domestic top-up tax from 1 January 2025, so Malaysia keeps the difference rather than gifting it overseas.
cards.d: A firm taxed below 15% in Malaysia now owes a top-up to reach it. If Putrajaya does not collect that gap, the company's home country can. The Finance Act 2023 brought in a domestic top-up tax (QDMTT) from 1 January 2025, so Malaysia keeps the difference rather than gifting it overseas.
sources: MIDA GMT page (QDMTT + IIR from 1 Jan 2025); HASIL Guidelines on the Implementation of GMT in Malaysia (Dec 2024); Finance Act (No. 2) 2023

cards.h: Penang's electronics and semiconductor cluster was built substantially on tax holidays that pushed effective rates far below the 24% headline.
cards.s: The 15% floor blunts that lure just as the US-China chip reshuffle makes Malaysia attractive for other reasons.
cards.d: Penang's electronics and semiconductor cluster was built substantially on tax holidays that pushed effective rates far below the 24% headline corporate rate. The 15% floor blunts that lure just as the US-China chip reshuffle makes Malaysia attractive for other reasons.
sources: MIDA incentive record (pioneer status / Investment Tax Allowance); Malaysia headline corporate rate 24%; Penang electronics FDI history

cards.h: Malaysia's answer is a New Incentive Framework that pays for results, not size, replacing profit-based holidays from 1 March 2026.
cards.s: Grants now hinge on jobs, technology transfer, and supply-chain depth, scored on a national scorecard, a 40-year shift made with little public debate.
cards.d: Malaysia's answer is a New Incentive Framework that pays for results, not size, replacing profit-based holidays from 1 March 2026. Grants now hinge on jobs, technology transfer, and supply-chain depth, scored on a national scorecard, a 40-year shift made with little public debate.
sources: MITI New Incentive Framework (effective 1 March 2026, NIA scorecard, STR/ITA); MIDA media release; KPMG NIF briefing

cards.text: The question is no longer how low Malaysia can set its tax rate. It is what the country offers once it no longer can.
It is like a duty-free shop that wakes to find the same tax now charged at the gate. The saving that pulled in the crowd is collected down the corridor instead.

Tax holidays were a race to the bottom that Malaysia could at least win. The floor ends that race and forces a harder question: whether the country competes on talent, power, and ports, or has nothing left to bid.

sources: MIDA (Implementation of GMT in Malaysia; New Incentive Framework media release); HASIL Guidelines on the Implementation of GMT in Malaysia (Dec 2024) + What is QDMTT; Finance Act (No. 2) 2023; MITI New Incentive Framework; OECD Pillar Two GloBE Model Rules; Crowe Malaysia; PwC Malaysia; US-ASEAN Business Council. See engine/briefs/global-minimum-tax-incentive-erosion.md.
confidence: High on mechanism and dates (GMT effective FY from 1 Jan 2025; 15% ETR; EUR 750M threshold; QDMTT + IIR; NIF effective 1 March 2026), all confirmed against the regulator/agency. Medium on the SCALE of impact, which is deliberately not quantified: no official figure for expected QDMTT revenue or for incentive-related forgone revenue was found, so no ringgit magnitude is asserted.
needs_verification: Finance Act (No. 2) 2023 gazette citation (29 Dec 2023) and the exact QDMTT/IIR provisions and effective date.
That pioneer status / Investment Tax Allowance historically pushed effective rates 'far below' 24% toward near-zero for favoured firms (characterisation, not a single number).
Whether a sourced forgone-revenue or tax-expenditure figure exists (MOF Economic Report / tax-expenditure statement) that could be added without overclaim.
source_notes: No official GMT revenue estimate was located; the cards therefore assert no ringgit magnitude. Effective rates under pioneer status vary by tier (70-100% income-tax exemption bands) and firm; the cards say 'far below the 24% headline' rather than a single figure. The US-China 'chip reshuffle' framing is general context, stated softly ('for other reasons').
